clue.text: Band in studio as I speak

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of 'studio', all of 'as' and 'I', and the start of 'speak'

explanation.surface: A musician talks about a band while sitting in the recording studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis is the Manchester rock band of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a famous British rock group, so 'Band' is a definition by example.

clue.text: Seeing Oscar bowled before hitting the first shot?

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
in tennis the opening shot of each point is the serve

explanation.surface: A tennis or cricket spectator watches a player who is out bowled just before starting a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the serve is being defined by a playful description rather than a dictionary one.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing is watching or noticing, a close synonym of seeing in its visual sense.

clue.text: Some tempest or monsoon?

indicators.note: 'Some' means only part of the following words is used, a stretch lying within them

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of 'tempest', the word 'or' and the first letter of 'monsoon'

explanation.surface: A question about wild weather: a tempest or perhaps a monsoon?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it hides the answer and also describes it, since a tempest or monsoon is a kind of violent weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm and a monsoon brings stormy rain, so both are examples of the answer.

clue.text: Gentleman concealing large fib is more foolhardy

indicators.note: concealing means holding something out of sight inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: sir is the polite address to a gentleman
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a fib is a small lie

explanation.surface: A gentleman covering up a big lie is behaving recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly can mean lacking good sense, so its comparative fits 'more foolhardy', meaning more rash.

clue.text: Compiler almost worried by an officer of the law

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole, so the final letter of the word is dropped
worried suggests being agitated and shaken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word taken as written, less its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is anxious after being questioned by a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler' reads as the setter talking about themself, as usual in crosswords, but here the word itself is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman is a member of the police force, an officer charged with enforcing the law.

clue.text: Claims we ignore women's wish

indicators.note: ignoring the women's part means the letter standing for women is left out

parts.note: pleas are claims or arguments put forward, as in court
the word taken as written with its W, the abbreviation for women, removed

explanation.surface: Someone says that they will set aside what the women want.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to wish or choose, as in 'do as you please'.

clue.text: Record in French — Edward paid attention

parts.note: to list is to record items in order
en is the French word for in
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward made a record in French and the audience paid attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Listened means heard carefully, which is to pay attention to what is being said.

clue.text: Gather mobile phone turned up in bed

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is flipped to read from bottom to top

parts.note: cell is short for cellphone, a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves a mobile that has surfaced among the bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect is to gather things together into one place.

clue.text: Grew angry about wound I feign

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: mad is a colloquial word for angry

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted round, means the letters are wrung into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone became furious about an injury they had been pretending to have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnified means made larger, which is close to grew in its transitive sense of increased.

clue.text: School upset with son's jottings

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means knocked over so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Parents are upset by what the school wrote about their son.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is a famous English boarding school, a staple of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written jottings made as a reminder.

clue.text: Bears ought to hear us oddly escaping

parts.note: should expresses what one ought to do

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters escaping, only the even-placed ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A plea that the bears should listen to us as we get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to carry or bear it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Illumination predicament with power cut

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the letter standing for power is taken out

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Being stuck in the dark during a power cut, with no illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Light is what illumination provides; the two are synonyms for brightness that lets us see.

clue.text: Stays saner? I'm mad!

indicators.note: mad means crazy and disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asked to stay calmer protests that they are actually mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains and stays are both verbs meaning continues to be in a place or state.

clue.text: I see men fighting adversaries

indicators.note: men fighting are in a scuffle, so the letters scramble into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An onlooker watches men brawling with their opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies are people who oppose you, so adversaries is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Guarantee cool treasure? Not half!

indicators.note: 'Not half' says the first half of the preceding word is thrown away

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
the word with its first four of eight letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stylish treasure is guaranteed, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so!', which hides its job of removing half a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to guarantee against loss by means of a policy.

clue.text: Delicate cuckoo nest is on island very close to home

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters following are scrambled

parts.note: the letters taken as written, then rearranged
I is a standard abbreviation for island
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fragile cuckoo's nest on an island lies very near the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the bird, fitting the nest, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitive can mean easily damaged or needing careful handling, the sense of delicate.

clue.text: Spot slender gymnast initially jumping up and down

parts.note: to spot is to see
slender means thin

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Watch the slim gymnast bounce up and down at the start of a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is figurative: jumping up and down with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Seething means boiling with fury, the state of someone metaphorically hopping mad.

clue.text: Male maybe leaving diamonds with friend, as a rule

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for diamonds goes out of the word

parts.note: male is an example of a gender, hence 'maybe'
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A man typically leaves his jewellery with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and 'as a rule' are both adverbs meaning usually, in most cases.

clue.text: Most picky female on American ship, I estimated

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
USS, United States Ship, prefixes the names of American naval vessels
taken as written
est. is the abbreviation for estimated

explanation.surface: A passenger guesses which woman aboard a US ship is the fussiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fussiest means hardest to please, the superlative of fussy, matching most picky.

clue.text: Charitable type describing short Greek god

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a genus is a type or class

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the god's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love; one letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A kindly sort of person giving an account of a minor Greek deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charitable type' looks like a noun phrase, but the definition stops at 'Charitable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous means free in giving, which is what being charitable involves.

clue.text: Vile beer drunk bishop will leave for free

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and confused, so the letters are rearranged
the bishop will leave, meaning his letter departs from the mix

parts.note: the letters taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop who has drunk nasty beer departs without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to free someone from a burden or duty, so the verbs match.

clue.text: What excuse?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the polite request to repeat something not heard
second meaning: to forgive an offence

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one question about an excuse; it is two separate words with one shared answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is said as 'what?' when you did not catch something, and as a verb it means to forgive or excuse.

clue.text: Measures adult horses

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
mounts are horses for riding

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up grown horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts and measures are both nouns for quantities of something.

clue.text: Vulgar description of trumpet's sound?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: showy and loud in a tasteless way
second meaning: having the blaring tone of a brass instrument

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second definition is a playful one: a trumpet is a brass instrument, so its sound is literally brass-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means flashy and coarse, and also harsh and blaring like brass instruments.

clue.text: Servant finally searches for unimportant things

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so just the last letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
to rifle through things is to search them hastily

explanation.surface: At last a servant goes looking for small trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifles are things of little value or importance.

clue.text: Group of soldiers also protecting king, quietly

indicators.note: protecting means shielding by surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: too means also
R for rex, Latin for king
p for piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Soldiers also guard the king, silently.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially in cavalry or artillery.

clue.text: Roll containing old chicken

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A bread roll filled with leftover chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' suggests bread, fitting the chicken, but here it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, so the definition is a broader class than the answer.

clue.text: Tense expression lifted before student's test

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means raised so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is an expression or look on a face
L for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A nervous look passes over a student's face before an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous but stands for the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test of quality or performance.

clue.text: Suggest operation in Spain

parts.note: op is short for operation
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Someone proposes having surgery in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, much as to suggest is to put forward a view.

clue.text: Key German city — it goes round a lake

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: goes round means turns about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A major German city with a lake that you can walk around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round a lake' looks like one piece circling another, but it only turns the small word over.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means crucial, so essential is a synonym.

clue.text: Soon begrudge interrupting work

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
to resent is to begrudge

explanation.surface: Before long, someone will resent being disturbed at their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently can mean shortly or in a little while, the same as soon.

clue.text: Witty remark perhaps entertaining two Liberals

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: say means for example, as perhaps does
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, twice

explanation.surface: A quip that might amuse a pair of Liberal politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick, clever retort, a crossword-favourite word for a witticism.
